audits.text:
## 524410ebe7b7

**Reproduced authority/domain mismatch.** Selected generator SHA-256: `1d4fb4463210e00edd4328d7d0d752ab97517bf6df833ceda4ec5e52958fb048`; executed canonical rule hash: `5d8d4dae083d`.

The selected summary and sampler teach “fill the interior of a complete hollow rectangle.” The Racket authority is broader: it fills any zero-region that does not touch the border and has exactly one nonzero neighbouring color. Consequently, a rectangle-only solver fits every canonical example and every ordinary selected-generator sample but is not the full authority.

`checks/audit/524410ebe7b7/input.json` contains one normal 3×3 color-3 frame plus a color-4 cross enclosing a single zero at `(3,7)`. The selected `self_check` returns `[]`. Racket fills both `(2,2)` with 3 and `(3,7)` with 4; the rectangle-only rival fills only `(2,2)`. The exact differing cell, hashes, command, domain note, and evidence links are in `checks/audit/524410ebe7b7/counterexample.json`; raw authority output is `checks/audit/524410ebe7b7/racket.json`.

The constructed input is validator-accepted but outside the summary's stated exactly-one-frame generator domain because it adds an irregular enclosure. That is itself part of the issue: validation admits broader authority cases while sampling and prose omit them. Suggested triage is to align the summary and generator with enclosed single-color regions and add nonrectangular/multiple-cavity examples, or explicitly narrow validation while documenting that the selected rule remains broader. I left the audited source unchanged.

audits.text:
## 524410ebe7b7

**Reproduced authority/domain mismatch from retained source-bound evidence.** The
audit source SHA-256
`1d4fb4463210e00edd4328d7d0d752ab97517bf6df833ceda4ec5e52958fb048`
matches the assignment. The generator/self-check describes complete hollow
rectangles, while the selected Racket authority fills any enclosed zero region
using a neighboring nonzero color. A retained lawful input combines a 3×3
color-3 frame with a color-4 cross-shaped cavity. `self_check` accepts it; the
Racket output fills both enclosed regions, whereas the rectangle-only rival
leaves cell `(3,7)` at 0 instead of 4.

Current-audit copies are in:
`checks/audit/524410ebe7b7/counterexample.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`,
`rival_output.json`, `probe.json`, and `verification.json`. Verification confirms
one differing cell `[3,7,0,4]`, no self-check errors, and source-hash parity. I did
not rerun Racket; `verification.json` identifies the immutable retained evidence
path and records that limitation.

Suggested resolution: either narrow the authority/domain to complete hollow
rectangles or broaden generation/self-check/notes to all enclosed regions and add
a nonrectangular cavity regression. Until then, do not treat rectangle-only
lesson evidence as full coverage of the executable rule. No source change or
approval action was performed.
